title: Fractional Surge Credit & Temp Hire Lifecycle Matrix
body:
Purpose
- Rapidly sketch an operational playbook that ties a small pool of fractional surge credits (prepaid compute credits) to a lifecycle of temporary talent (contractors, fractional FTEs, short-term hires) so we can respond to token-demand spikes without long-term headcount commitments.
- Surface sensitivity to small incremental changes in per-token list price and reserved-capacity discounts so finance + product can set thresholds for when to convert surge-to-hire or throttle pricing.

Key constraints and assumptions (summary)
- Base runway assumption: $72M cash, 18 months runway at baseline burn (May 2026).
- Baseline avg token price to customers: $0.0008 / token.
- Cost to serve (average across model mix) today: $0.00035 / token (includes GPU amortization, infra, ops alloc).
- Fractional surge credit pool: $250k prepaid, regionally distributed (NA/EU/APAC split 60/30/10). Credits convert to ~715M tokens of variable-cost capacity at baseline.
- Two workforce ladders: (A) Contractors (3 month avg engagement, blended fully-loaded rate $12k/mo), (B) Fractional FTEs (0.25–0.6 FTE; blended $6k/mo per 0.25 FTE).
- Decision window: daily monitoring; convert surge credits to contractor slots when 7-day rolling token demand exceeds forecast by >35% AND expected incremental margin > 30%.

Playbook: lifecycle stages
1) Detect surge (SLO)
   - Trigger: 7d rolling token volume > forecast * 1.35 OR 95th-percentile latency SLO breach for >3 hours.
   - Data inputs: token telemetry, per-route margin, cost-to-serve by model, regional capacity utilization.
2) Activate fractional surge credits (auto)
   - Immediate: burn prepaid credits to provide compute headroom; rate limit non-critical routes to preserve credits until human review.
   - Duration target: <72 hours of credit draw while assessing ramp shape.
3) Fast-staff decision (Handoff to finance+ops)
   - If surge appears persistent (>5 rolling days), propose contractor engagements: allocate up to 12 contractor slots (3-week sourcing lead) to 1) optimize model mix, 2) implement heavier caching, 3) tune batch sizes.
   - Finance check: incremental revenue run-rate required to justify contractor spend = contractor fully-loaded cost / expected incremental monthly gross margin.
4) Convert to fractional FTE or permanent hire
   - If after 6 weeks the new baseline token level > forecast by >20% and projected 6-month incremental margin > 50%: convert top-performing contractors to fractional FTEs or open perm reqs.

Sample sensitivity scenarios (concise)
- Scenario A (shallow spike): +40% tokens for 4 days, median latencies up 15%
  - Credits consumed: ~110M tokens -> $38.5k of cost (net of reserved-discount)
  - Contractor ramp: not triggered (decision threshold 5 days)
  - Net margin on incremental revenue (if priced at flat list): 56% (profitable to serve)

- Scenario B (sustained elevated demand): +60% tokens for 28 days
  - Credits consumed if used immediately: ~600M tokens (~$210k cost) -> exceeds pool; triggers contractor conversion on day 6
  - Contractor cost (12 slots x $12k/mo x 1 mo): $144k (first month), expected incremental revenue at baseline list price: $420k -> incremental gross margin ~66% after contractor spending in month 1
  - Sensitivity to price drop: if list price compresses 20% (to $0.00064/token), incremental revenue falls to $336k and margin falls to ~49%: borderline for perm hires, still OK for contractors 1–2 months while monitoring

- Scenario C (price-led erosion): +50% tokens for 10 days but list price declines 25% due to market pressure
  - Expected reaction: restrict non-essential routes, prioritize high-margin customers, push rate-limit thresholds.
  - Convert credits to targeted peering/region bursts only; avoid broad contractor onboarding until 7d trend confirms sustained uptake

Budget model (simple table, flattened)
- Inputs: baseline tokens/mo = 5,000M; baseline revenue/mo = baseline tokens * $0.0008 = $4,000,000
- Incremental delta example (Sustained +60%): incremental tokens = 3,000M; incremental list rev = 3,000M * $0.0008 = $2,400,000/mo
- Incremental cost to serve (at $0.00035 cost): 3,000M * $0.00035 = $1,050,000
- Contractor headcount (month 1) cost = 12 * $12,000 = $144,000
- Fractional FTEs (if convert) typical monthly = 6 * $12,000 (equivalent) = $72,000
- Net incremental gross margin (month 1 w/ contractors) = 2,400,000 - 1,050,000 - 144,000 = $1,206,000 (~50% of combined revenue)

Decision thresholds (finance knobs)
- Credit pool top-up rules: auto-top-up to maintain 25% pool if forecasted 30-day utilization > 70% of pool and expected gross margin on incremental rev > 45%.
- Contractor approval gate: PO auto for up to $200k; above that requires finance director sign-off.
- Convert-to-hire gate: sustained 6-week delta > 20% and 6-month rolling incremental gross contribution > 50% of ramped costs.

Runway and headcount impact (quick projection)
- If we historically convert 50% of sustained surges to perm hires, the model shows incremental headcount of +8–14 FTE over 12 months under moderate growth; incremental opex increases ~3.4% (runway reduction ~0.7 months).
- If instead we rely on contractors + credits, runway impact is smaller (~0.2 months) but unit cost per token remains higher in steady state.

Risks and mitigations
- Risk: Credits exhausted in region during simultaneous spikes -> mitigation: regional fair-share quota + auto-fallback to lower-cost model variants.
- Risk: Market price compression leads to negative margin during long-lasting surge -> mitigation: early rate-limits, whitelisting, and fast discounted billing adjustments for large enterprise customers.
- Operational: Sourcing lag for contractors -> mitigation: maintain bench of pre-approved contractors (legal/ID cleared) and 2-day onboarding template.

Open questions for next iteration
- Should we index credit pool top-ups to a rolling 90d moving average of token volatility rather than fixed thresholds?
- What SLA delta warranting permanent hires vs contractor recycling is acceptable to Sales (customer PS impact)?
- Can we automate an excursion-report that ties token surge to route-level profitability in near-real-time?

Action items (next 3 weeks)
- Finance: build 2-way sensitivity tab in workbook (Priya to own) capturing list-price compression (0/10/20/30%) and reserve-discount tiers (0/10/20%) -> due 2026-06-09.
- Ops: assemble bench of 20 pre-approved contractor profiles (SRE, infra, perf-engineer) -> Omar to lead, due 2026-06-16.
- Product: implement per-route margin tagging in metrics pipeline (quick tag to enable whitelisting during surge) -> Sofia to coordinate with metrics, due 2026-06-23.

Notes to reviewer
- This is intentionally compact; follow-up sheet will include line-item cashflow sims, burn curves, and a Monte-Carlo sampler over volatility and price-compression.
- Want feedback on the tolerances for margin thresholds (50% vs 45%) and whether to treat fractional FTEs as capex-like commitments for conversion logic.

Appendix (quick glossary)
- Fractional surge credits: prepaid compute credits used for short-term capacity bursts.
- Fractional FTE: partial FTE engagements (0.25–0.6) billed monthly; used to retain specialized skills without perm ramp.
- Reserved-discount: negotiated savings when committing to reserved capacity; impacts cost-to-serve in sensitivity model.

End of doc.
